title: Chip Industry Week In Review
gist: This weekly roundup reports export controls tightening around China and Southeast Asia: Commerce rules on overseas remote access, TSMC reportedly limiting affected Chinese customers to 28/40nm, and Nvidia guiding to zero China data center revenue. Meanwhile, Nvidia-led AI demand is driving packaging capacity deals (SPIL to triple Taiwan capacity by mid-2029). Intel Foundry won its first external 18A-P customer and an EMIB deal with Microsoft, Siemens is buying Breker, and JEDEC previewed DDR6.

insights.claim: Intel Foundry has signed its first external customer for its 18A-P process, according to Intel executives. The customer has not been named and Intel has not given a production timetable.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: This validates Intel's external foundry strategy, but with no named customer or timeline the revenue impact is still unquantifiable. Watch for the customer to be disclosed.
insights.quote: The customer has not been identified, and Intel has not disclosed a production timetable.
insights.locator: Intel Foundry signed its first external customer

insights.claim: Microsoft picked Intel Foundry's EMIB advanced packaging for custom silicon in Azure infrastructure. The multiyear deal also widens cooperation on Xeon processors, memory and security technologies.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: A hyperscaler choosing EMIB makes it a credible alternative to TSMC CoWoS packaging for custom AI and cloud silicon, which supports Intel's packaging-led foundry revenue.

insights.claim: Nvidia widened its manufacturing agreements with Amkor, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, SPIL, TSMC and others to cover more substrate manufacturing, advanced packaging and wafer capacity.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Nvidia is locking up the supply of substrates and packaging, which points to long demand visibility. OSATs and substrate makers benefit, and competitors may find capacity harder to get.

insights.claim: ASE subsidiary SPIL signed a multibillion-dollar agreement with Nvidia to triple its advanced packaging capacity in Taiwan by mid-2029. The deal includes new production lines for wafer bumping, assembly and test.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Tripling capacity by 2029 under a single-customer commitment gives ASE/SPIL multi-year revenue visibility and shows advanced packaging is still a bottleneck for AI.
insights.quote: triple its advanced semiconductor packaging capacity in Taiwan by mid-2029
insights.locator: As part of the expansion, ASE subsidiary SPIL

insights.claim: ASE Technology opened the first phase of its Lujhu advanced packaging facility in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, and started building the second phase.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: More evidence of OSAT capex going into advanced packaging in Taiwan, which supports equipment demand for back-end tool vendors.
insights.locator: ASE Technology inaugurated the first phase

insights.claim: Kulicke & Soffa shipped its first fluxless thermocompression bonding systems for panel-level packaging to two customers in Taiwan. The tools target larger, denser packages for AI and HPC chips.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Panel-level packaging is moving from R&D into tool shipments, a potential new growth leg for K&S on top of its recovering revenue.
insights.locator: Kulicke & Soffa shipped its first fluxless

insights.claim: Silicon Box has moved its proposed packaging and test facility in Novara, Italy, into the basic design stage. The goal is more European advanced packaging capacity for chiplet-based devices.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Europe's chiplet packaging capacity is still at the design stage, so meaningful output is years away.

insights.claim: GlobalFoundries broke ground on a new 300mm fab in Malta, New York, under a U.S.-Japan investment initiative that provides up to $21B for two fabs. The first 300mm fab is expected to start production in 2029.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Up to $21B in co-funded capacity strengthens GF's onshoring story, but the 2029 start means revenue impact is long-dated.
insights.quote: The first 300mm fab is expected to begin production in 2029.
insights.locator: GlobalFoundries broke ground on a new 300mm

insights.claim: Lam Research broke ground on a technology center in Zhunan, Taiwan, as part of a five-year, $3B global R&D expansion.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Lam is investing R&D close to its leading Taiwanese customers, which supports its position in etch and deposition at advanced nodes.
insights.locator: Lam Research broke ground on a technology center

insights.claim: SK hynix detailed a jointly funded ₩874.6B (US$655M) semiconductor test facility at its Yongin complex in South Korea, with the cleanroom scheduled to open in May 2027.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Spending on test capacity points to SK hynix preparing for higher HBM and memory output volumes, a positive for test equipment vendors.

insights.claim: ACM Research opened a research and manufacturing facility in Hillsboro, Oregon, to develop and produce its wet-cleaning and electroplating equipment in the U.S.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: A U.S. manufacturing footprint could reduce ACM's geopolitical exposure as a China-linked equipment vendor.
insights.locator: ACM Research opened a new research

insights.claim: ADEKA and Entegris agreed to collaborate on producing advanced semiconductor materials in Japan.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Part of a broader trend of localizing materials supply chains in Japan.

insights.claim: General Flash raised $128M to scale production of critical metals used in semiconductors and other industries.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Investors are funding supply of critical metals for chips, which reflects concern about access to critical minerals.

insights.claim: GlobalFoundries and Boston Dynamics are deploying autonomous Spot inspection robots across GF fabs in the U.S., Germany and Singapore. GF also plans to start evaluating Atlas humanoid robots for semiconductor manufacturing tasks in early 2027.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Fabs are an early commercial testbed for humanoid robots. Watch the 2027 Atlas evaluation as a signal for robotics adoption in factories.

insights.claim: The U.S. Commerce Department introduced restrictions on remote access to advanced U.S. AI compute through overseas data centers. It also added semiconductor licensing requirements affecting Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: This closes the cloud-access and transshipment loopholes. Demand for AI chips and data centers in Southeast Asia now faces licensing friction, which may slow shipments to those regions.
insights.locator: The U.S. Department of Commerce introduced

insights.claim: U.S. government data show license requests covering 3.4 million advanced Nvidia and AMD AI chips for China, of which more than 879,000 were approved. It is unclear how many actually shipped.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Roughly a quarter of the requested volume was approved, which bounds the theoretical China AI-chip revenue pool, but actual shipments are unknown.

insights.claim: TSMC and Samsung reportedly suspended some chip shipments to Chinese customers pending licensing approvals under new U.S. export rules, per the Financial Times. TSMC is reportedly halting affected Chinese orders at 16nm and below without U.S. approval and generally limiting those customers to 28nm and 40nm, as long as the chips do not use HBM or advanced packaging.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: A de facto 16nm ceiling for affected Chinese customers at TSMC hits Chinese AI and fabless designers and pushes demand toward domestic foundries such as SMIC.
insights.quote: generally limiting those customers to 28nm and 40nm processes, provided those chips do not use HBM or advanced packaging

insights.claim: Per the NYT, Nvidia put Megaspeed on its no-sell list in June 2025, but Megaspeed's Malaysian subsidiary Speedmatrix later received more than $800M of Nvidia AI technology, mostly through third-party manufacturers. The U.S. government is investigating suspected export-control violations, and Nvidia says it blocked new orders.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: This shows indirect channels can route around vendor no-sell lists. It raises the compliance risk for Nvidia and explains the tighter Malaysia licensing rules.
insights.quote: Speedmatrix, later received more than $800M in Nvidia AI technology, mostly through third-party manufacturers
insights.locator: The U.S. government released new details

insights.claim: Reuters reports the Trump administration is moving toward restrictions on Chinese optical transceiver imports despite opposition from major U.S. cloud companies.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Restricting Chinese optics could raise hyperscaler networking costs and benefit non-Chinese transceiver suppliers.
insights.locator: The Trump administration is moving toward

insights.claim: On its earnings call, Nvidia said it has stopped shipping licensed Hopper AI chips to China, and its Q4 outlook assumes no data center compute revenue from China. Nvidia also created an oversight committee for national security policy, export-control compliance and global trade risk.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: China data center revenue is now zero in Nvidia's guidance, so any reopening would be upside. The new committee reflects rising regulatory exposure.
insights.quote: its Q4 outlook assumes no data center compute revenue from China
insights.locator: Notable: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress

insights.claim: The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission says China still trails in leading-edge fabrication, HBM and chip-making equipment. China is working around those gaps through DUV multi-patterning, advanced packaging, 3D stacking and photonics.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
entities: US-China Economic and Security Review Commission
insights.so_what: China's workaround path runs through packaging, stacking and photonics, so future export-control targets are likely to move into those areas.

insights.claim: A CSIS report on the risks of Chinese memory chips, including CXMT DRAM, cites security and supply-chain concerns. It recommends restricting their use in sensitive government systems and expanding independent chip testing.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: A possible policy precedent for restricting CXMT DRAM in Western procurement, which would favor Micron, Samsung and SK hynix in sensitive markets.

insights.claim: At SC26, Nvidia announced a Rubin HPC GPU with more than 50,000 CUDA cores and sparse data acceleration. It also announced a 192-CPU Vera rack-scale HPC platform with more than 200TB/s of aggregate peak memory bandwidth.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Nvidia is pushing deeper into traditional HPC and CPU-heavy systems, putting competitive pressure on AMD and x86 in supercomputing.
insights.locator: Nvidia announced a Rubin HPC GPU

insights.claim: Lambda is deploying Nvidia's co-packaged optics (CPO) switches to connect GB300 NVL72 racks totaling more than 10,000 GPUs. Nvidia claims up to 5x better power efficiency and 15x higher reliability than conventional pluggable optics.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: CPO is entering production deployments, a threat to the pluggable transceiver business and an opportunity for photonics suppliers.
insights.locator: Lambda is deploying Nvidia's CPO switches

insights.claim: Penguin Solutions unveiled a photonics-based, HBM-class memory appliance that uses Marvell technology to let CPUs and GPUs share memory across servers.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: An early sign that memory disaggregation over optics could become a new category for Marvell and photonics vendors.

insights.claim: Infineon and Megmeet are partnering on 800V DC power architectures for AI data centers, using Infineon's gen-2 CoolSiC MOSFETs in three-phase power shelves.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: The move to 800V DC in AI racks gives silicon carbide a data center end market beyond EVs, which supports SiC volume for Infineon.
insights.locator: Infineon and Megmeet are teaming up

insights.claim: Uppsala University researchers proposed using co-packaged optics to broadcast LLM weights from centralized memory, reducing the amount of HBM needed.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: If architectures like this mature, they could reduce HBM content per accelerator, a long-dated risk to the HBM demand thesis.

insights.claim: Researchers at UC Irvine and Samsung Electronics created topology-optimized liquid-cooling cold plates to reduce thermal crosstalk between AI processors and HBM.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Thermal coupling between logic and HBM is a real design constraint, and liquid-cooling component vendors benefit.
insights.locator: Researchers at UC Irvine and Samsung

insights.claim: AMD finished acquiring AI inference chip developer Taalas and AI model research company World Labs.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: AMD is building out inference silicon and AI model capabilities through M&A to compete with Nvidia.

insights.claim: Microsoft made its Azure Cobalt 200 virtual machines, based on Arm Neoverse CSS V3, generally available for cloud and AI workloads.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler in-house Arm CPUs take share from x86 server CPUs and add Arm royalty revenue.

insights.claim: TrendForce expects NAND flash contract prices to fall in 2027 as Chinese cloud providers cut enterprise SSD orders because of GPU shortages and high inventories. Global NAND capex is still projected to rise about 27% to about US$30B.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Falling prices while capex rises is a classic oversupply setup, bearish for NAND pricing and margins in 2027.
insights.quote: NAND flash contract prices are expected to decline in 2027
insights.locator: NAND flash contract prices are expected

insights.claim: JEDEC previewed the DDR6 specification, which is still subject to change. The current plan includes higher data rates, a wider bus, a pseudo-channel architecture, optimizations for die stacking and high-capacity modules, and low-power modes aimed at data centers.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: DDR6 is designed with stacking and data center use in mind, which points to higher content and ASPs per module for DRAM makers and interface chip vendors.

insights.claim: JEDEC started a System Level Reliability Testing subcommittee to develop qualification methods, reliability practices and evaluation approaches for emerging system applications.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Standardizing system-level reliability testing could expand the test market.
insights.locator: JEDEC also started a System Level

themes.theme: AI in chip design, EDA and test

insights.claim: Siemens plans to buy Breker Verification Systems, which develops AI-driven test suite synthesis and system-level verification. The deal is expected to close in December.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Consolidation in EDA verification continues. Siemens is adding AI verification capability to compete with Synopsys and Cadence.

insights.claim: OpenAI reported progress in AI-assisted chip design, including RTL generation and design optimization for AMD processors and RISC-V cores. It is also working with Synopsys to train AI models to use EDA tools.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: AI model labs are moving into chip design workflows. Working with Synopsys suggests EDA incumbents will partner rather than be displaced, but tool pricing models could shift.

insights.claim: Advantest added the EXA Scale QX test head to its V93000 EXA Scale platform for high-power, high-pin-count AI and HPC devices. Its four-card-cage architecture provides 36 instrument slots, and it stays compatible with existing V93000 instruments, probers and handlers. Availability is expected in Q1 FY2027.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: AI chips need more test capacity, which supports Advantest's SoC tester growth. Backward compatibility protects its installed base.

insights.claim: Siemens and Microsoft plan to bring Simcenter X to Azure so engineering teams in automotive and other industries can run multi-domain simulations and scale HPC workloads in the cloud.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Engineering simulation is moving to the cloud, which shifts toward subscription revenue.

insights.claim: A KAIST team built a clock distribution network with a backside clock mesh in a backside power delivery (BSPDN) architecture. It showed 26% lower maximum local clock latency, 40% smaller global skew and 29% less mesh switching power on average than a frontside baseline.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Using the backside for clock as well as power adds to the value of backside power delivery at advanced nodes such as 18A and A16.
insights.quote: 26% lower maximum local clock latency, 40% smaller global skew, and 29% less mesh switching power on average than the frontside baseline
insights.locator: A KAIST team created a clock distribution

insights.claim: Tampere University and University of Southampton researchers developed wafer-scale ferroelectric transistors using MoS2 and hafnium-zirconium oxide (HZO) for nonvolatile, multibit memory. Nanjing University researchers separately built CMOS circuits from 2D MoS2 and 1D carbon nanotube transistors.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Low-dimensional materials are moving toward wafer-scale processing, a long-term option on scaling beyond silicon.

insights.claim: AMD disclosed a critical Platform Security Processor (PSP) boot ROM vulnerability in Zen/Zen+ processors. It can let attacker-controlled firmware bypass secure boot and run unsigned code with full PSP privileges, and AMD will not release a mitigation because the boot ROM cannot be modified.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: The flaw is unpatchable, so the installed base of older Zen systems is permanently exposed, which could speed up enterprise refresh cycles.
insights.quote: AMD does not plan to release a mitigation because the vulnerable boot ROM cannot be modified.
insights.locator: AMD disclosed a critical Platform Security

insights.claim: Intel issued a security announcement on a DDR5 rowhammer attack that researchers used to bypass certain protections, cause bit flips on systems with 12th- and 13th-gen Core processors, and escalate privileges.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Rowhammer still affects DDR5, which supports demand for in-DRAM mitigations and memory-security IP.

insights.claim: University of Luxembourg researchers found two timing side channels in Nvidia GPU load/store units that allowed full AES-128 key recovery and covert communication between processes under Nvidia's Multi-Process Service (MPS).
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Shared GPU tenancy carries side-channel risk, which matters for multi-tenant AI cloud isolation and pricing.

insights.claim: University of Kansas and Cornell researchers demonstrated a practical memory denial-of-service attack that slowed DDR5- and HBM2E-based systems by more than 1,000x while using less than 1 GB/s of memory bandwidth.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Low-bandwidth memory DoS threatens shared infrastructure and could drive memory-controller QoS features.
insights.quote: more than 1,000× slowdowns on DDR5- and HBM2E-based systems while consuming less than 1 GB/s of memory bandwidth
insights.locator: University of Kansas and Cornell researchers

insights.claim: SEALSQ signed a non-binding letter of intent to buy Australia-based QuintessenceLabs, combining secure chips with quantum random number generation and enterprise key management.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Consolidation in post-quantum security. The deal is non-binding, so the probability of closing is uncertain.

insights.claim: Altera, OQC and Nvidia demonstrated an FPGA-based quantum controller that uses an Agilex 9 Direct RF FPGA to connect a superconducting QPU to Nvidia GPUs for real-time control and readout. The design reduces the need for external RF conversion hardware.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: FPGAs gain a role in quantum control, and Nvidia is placing itself as the classical hub for quantum computing.

insights.claim: Quantum Machines showed real-time quantum error-correction processing with its OPX1000 controller and Nvidia CUDA-Q over NVQLink, reaching 2.4 microseconds of round-trip latency with a CPU-based decoder on simulated error data. GPU-based decoding is planned.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Microsecond-scale decoding loops are a prerequisite for fault-tolerant quantum computing, and Nvidia's NVQLink is becoming the default integration layer.

insights.claim: IBM, Nvidia and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory plan a quantum-classical co-design platform that pairs IBM quantum computers with Nvidia DGX B200 systems. Atom Computing separately finalized a CHIPS Act R&D award of up to $100M for neutral-atom quantum computers.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Public funding and hybrid quantum-HPC platforms point to quantum being integrated into supercomputing roadmaps.

insights.claim: The European Commission said more than 20 semiconductor projects have been approved under the EU Chips Act, representing more than €33B in public and private investment.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: European chip investment is progressing, which supports equipment demand and regional players such as Infineon and Soitec.

insights.claim: Year-over-year revenue growth reported: Keysight Q4 up 40%, Kulicke & Soffa Q4 up 131%, Nvidia Q3 up 103%, and Soitec Q2 up 50% at constant currency.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Strong growth across test, back-end equipment and substrates shows AI demand spreading beyond GPUs.

insights.claim: Science Corporation raised $400M for a retinal implant chip that aims to restore form vision for some types of macular degeneration.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: A large private round for neural and medical implant silicon, a niche but growing end market.

insights.claim: Cirrus Logic President/CEO John Forsyth was elected chair of the Semiconductor Industry Association, succeeding AMD CEO Lisa Su. GlobalFoundries Executive Chairman Tom Caulfield was elected vice chair. The UK separately opened applications for a £2.4M open-source semiconductor security program.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: The SIA leadership change could shift the industry's lobbying focus, including on export controls.
